notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-09/10. Oct 9-10 was a genuinely quiet announcement window across all four lanes — no lane found a reliably-sourced same-day item, so zero `announcement`-kind entries this run. Most forward-looking candidates each lane surfaced (CES 2027, MWC Barcelona 2027, NVIDIA GTC 2027, KubeCon Europe 2027, RSA Conference 2027, Colorado SB 26-189, Kubernetes 1.36/1.37 maintenance-mode dates, Amazon EKS 1.32 extended support, Microsoft Ignite 2026, AWS re:Invent 2026) were cross-checked against the full corpus and turned out to already be filed at equal or better confidence — this routine is now mostly rediscovering the same well-known dates each day, which is expected as the calendar fills in. Filed only the handful of genuinely new, well-sourced finds: a third distinct California AI-companion-chatbot law, a newly-dated security conference, two devtools/cloud lifecycle dates, and one hardware ship date.
concerns: The bigtech lane could not find any '$40B' figure backing the already-filed 'New Mexico seeks up to $40B penalty against Meta/Facebook after privacy-practices jury verdict' (2026-10-01). It found instead a confirmed New Mexico court ruling on 2026-08-06 ordering Meta to pay $567M on top of a $375M March 2026 verdict ($942M cumulative), a figure two orders of magnitude smaller. Not changed by me since I can't independently verify which figure is current or whether these are different stages of the same case — a maintainer should check primary court records before the next 2026-10-20 ruling-expected entry is touched.

Istio 1.30's end-of-life date is given as 2026-11-30 by endoflife.date but only as 'expected ~December 2026, pending Istio 1.32's release' by endoflife.ai — a real conflict between two otherwise-reliable trackers, not just a confidence question. Not filed rather than pick one. Also sits only ~49 days after the already-filed 'Istio 1.29 reaches end of life' (2026-10-12), the same version-number title-collision pattern flagged in prior runs' concerns — worth using a title that clearly spells out '1.30' if/when a maintainer files it.
